question: Earth’s core is mainly made up of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is nickel and iron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth's core is mainly composed of nickel and iron (NiFe), often referred to by the chemical symbol "Nife". (पृथ्वी की क्रोड — निकल और लोहा)

 

• The core has two parts: the inner core (solid, due to immense pressure) and the outer core (liquid), and it is this molten, convecting outer core that generates the Earth's magnetic field.

 

• The core is the innermost and densest layer of the Earth, extending from a depth of about 2,900 km to the centre at about 6,371 km.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The layer surrounding the core is the mantle, made mostly of silicate rocks rich in iron and magnesium, and the outermost solid layer is the thin crust.

 

• The study of the Earth's interior and its composition is estimated indirectly through the analysis of seismic waves.

 

NOTE

 

• Nickel and copper (Option 1): Copper is not a major constituent of the Earth's core.

 

• Nickel and alumina (Option 2): Alumina (aluminium oxide) is associated with the crust, not the dense metallic core.

 

• Nickel and magnesium (Option 4): Magnesium is a major component of the mantle, not the core.

question: The subject of the Study of Macro Economics is based on which principle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The principle of National Income.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Macroeconomics is the branch of economics that studies the economy as a whole, focusing on aggregate variables such as national income, output, employment and price level. (समष्टि अर्थशास्त्र — राष्ट्रीय आय का सिद्धांत)

 

• Its central concern is the measurement and determination of National Income, since national income accounting captures the overall performance of an economy in a given period.

 

• Macroeconomics thus deals with aggregates like GDP, GNP, NNP and total employment, rather than the behaviour of individual consumers or firms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term 'Macroeconomics' was coined by the Norwegian economist Ragnar Frisch in 1933, while modern macroeconomics is largely built on the work of John Maynard Keynes.

 

• Microeconomics, in contrast, studies individual economic units such as a consumer, household or firm.

 

NOTE

 

• The principle of Consumer (Option 2): Study of individual consumer behaviour falls under microeconomics, not macroeconomics.

 

• The principle of Producer (Option 3): Study of an individual producer/firm's decisions also falls under microeconomics.

 

• The principle of Investment (Option 4): Investment is only one of several macroeconomic variables; it is not the defining principle of the subject as a whole.

question: Who has been appointed as new National e-Governance Division CEO in March 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abhishek Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abhishek Singh, an IAS officer, was appointed as the CEO of the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) and MyGov India in March 2022, in addition to his role as CEO of Digital India Corporation. (राष्ट्रीय ई-गवर्नेंस प्रभाग — अभिषेक सिंह)

 

• NeGD functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and provides support for the implementation of the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP).

 

• He took over the role from his predecessor to steer key digital governance initiatives including MyGov, Digital India and related citizen-centric platforms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NeGD was set up to assist in policy formulation, programme management, and capacity building for e-governance projects across ministries and states.

 

• MeitY is also the nodal ministry for initiatives like Digital India, Aadhaar (through UIDAI coordination) and IT/ITeS promotion.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitin Chugh (Option 1): He is a banking sector executive, formerly MD & CEO of Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, unrelated to this NeGD appointment.

 

• Rajiv Kumar (Option 2): Rajiv Kumar is a name associated with other public roles (such as NITI Aayog or the Election Commission), not this NeGD appointment.

 

• TS Ramakrishnan (Option 4): Not the officer appointed to this post in March 2022.

question: The Durga temple at Aihole, built about ______ years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1400.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Durga temple at Aihole, in Karnataka, was built about 1400 years ago, during the rule of the Chalukyas of Badami, around the 7th–8th century CE. (दुर्गा मंदिर, ऐहोल — चालुक्य वंश)

 

• It is notable for its unique apsidal (horseshoe-shaped) plan, resembling a Buddhist chaitya hall, with a curved rear wall and a surrounding covered ambulatory passage (pradakshinapatha).

 

• Aihole, along with nearby Badami and Pattadakal, is considered a cradle of Indian temple architecture, showcasing the experimental phase of early Chalukyan temple building.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The temple, despite its name, is not originally dedicated to goddess Durga — the name comes from its proximity to the 'Durg' (fort) of the old town.

 

• Pattadakal, near Aihole, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with temples in both Dravidian and Nagara styles.

 

NOTE

 

• 1700 (Option 1): Overstates the temple's age; it dates to about the 7th–8th century CE, not earlier.

 

• 2000 (Option 2): Also overstates the age of this Chalukyan-era temple.

 

• 1100 (Option 3): Understates the temple's age; it is older than this figure.

question: According to the Brihat Samhita, what do you call the process of making scents, mouth perfumes and bath powders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhayukli (Gandhayukti).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Brihat Samhita, an encyclopaedic Sanskrit work by the astronomer-scholar Varahamihira (6th century CE), devotes a chapter titled 'Gandhayukti' to the art and science of preparing perfumes, scents, mouth fresheners and bath powders. (गन्धयुक्ति — वराहमिहिर, बृहत्संहिता)

 

• This chapter (traditionally numbered around Chapter 76–77 of the Brihat Samhita) describes formulations and recipes for fragrant compounds used in ancient India.

 

• Varahamihira is also celebrated for his other major works, the Pancha-Siddhantika and Brihat Jataka, covering astronomy and astrology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brihat Samhita is a wide-ranging text covering astronomy, astrology, architecture (vastu), horticulture, gemology and perfumery, reflecting the breadth of classical Indian scientific literature.

 

• Varahamihira lived and worked at Ujjain, an important centre of astronomical study in ancient India.

 

NOTE

 

• Jatuka (Option 1): Not the term used for this process in the Brihat Samhita.

 

• Kamplcica (Option 3): Not a recognised term from the text for perfumery.

 

• Pattanga (Option 4): Refers to a dye/plant (red sandalwood-related term) in some classical texts, not to the process of making perfumes.

question: Which organic compound has the structure R−COOH, with R referring to the alkyl, alkenyl, aryl, or other group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carboxylic acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A carboxylic acid is an organic compound containing a carboxyl group (–COOH) attached to an R group (alkyl, alkenyl, aryl or other), with the general formula R–COOH. (कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल — R-COOH)

 

• The carboxyl group itself combines a carbonyl (C=O) and a hydroxyl (–OH) group on the same carbon atom, making carboxylic acids acidic due to the ionisable hydrogen of the –OH.

 

• Common examples include formic acid (HCOOH), acetic acid (CH₃COOH), and benzoic acid (C₆H₅COOH).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Carboxylic acids react with alcohols in the presence of an acid catalyst to form esters, in a reaction called esterification.

 

• Fatty acids, which make up fats and oils, are long-chain carboxylic acids.

 

NOTE

 

• Ester (Option 2): General structure is R–COO–R′ (formed from an acid and an alcohol), not R–COOH.

 

• Ketone (Option 3): General structure is R–CO–R′, with the carbonyl group between two carbon chains, no –OH group.

 

• Aldehydes (Option 4): General structure is R–CHO, with the carbonyl group at the end of the chain, not R–COOH.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India authorises the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in specific categories of matters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 143.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 143 of the Constitution deals with the 'Power of President to consult Supreme Court', allowing the President to seek the Supreme Court's opinion on questions of law or fact of public importance, or on certain pre-Constitution disputes/treaties. (अनुच्छेद 143 — राष्ट्रपति की परामर्शदाता शक्ति)

 

• This is known as the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court; the Court's opinion under this Article is not binding on the President, unlike its judgments in regular cases.

 

• A notable instance of its use was the Presidential Reference in the Ayodhya title dispute (1993).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 141 makes the law declared by the Supreme Court binding on all courts within India.

 

• Article 137 empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgments/orders.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 144 (Option 1): Requires all civil and judicial authorities in India to act in aid of the Supreme Court.

 

• Article 145 (Option 2): Deals with the rules made by the Supreme Court for regulating its own practice and procedure.

 

• Article 142 (Option 3): Empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree/order necessary for doing complete justice in any matter before it.

question: The ‘flag-raising’ ceremony by the Prime Minister of India on Independence Day is held at which of the following places in Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red Fort.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On Independence Day (15 August), the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag and addresses the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi. (लाल किला — स्वतंत्रता दिवस ध्वजारोहण)

 

• This tradition began on 15 August 1947, when Jawaharlal Nehru, independent India's first Prime Minister, hoisted the flag at the Red Fort.

 

• The Red Fort was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and served as the main residence of Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In contrast, on Republic Day (26 January), the flag is hoisted by the President of India, and the main parade traditionally takes place along Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath).

 

• The Red Fort was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

 

NOTE

 

• Old Fort (Option 1): (Purana Qila) is a separate historic fort in Delhi, not the Independence Day flag-hoisting venue.

 

• Parliament House (Option 2): Seat of India's legislature, not used for this ceremony.

 

• Rashtrapati Bhavan (Option 3): The President's official residence; the President addresses the nation on the eve of Republic Day and Independence Day from here, but the flag-hoisting ceremony itself is at the Red Fort.

question: The British Parliament transferred the powers of the East India company to the British crown in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1858.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Following the Revolt of 1857, the British Parliament passed the Government of India Act, 1858, which transferred the administration of India from the East India Company to the British Crown. (भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1858 — ब्रिटिश ताज को सत्ता हस्तांतरण)

 

• This period is known as the beginning of direct Crown rule (British Raj) in India, ending Company rule.

 

• The Act created the post of Secretary of State for India, who was to be assisted by an advisory council, replacing the Company's Court of Directors and Board of Control.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Canning was the Governor-General at the time and became the first Viceroy of India under Crown rule.

 

• Queen Victoria's proclamation of 1 November 1858 at Allahabad formally announced the transfer of power.

 

NOTE

 

• 1856 (Option 1): Not the year of transfer; this was before the 1857 revolt.

 

• 1854 (Option 3): Also predates the transfer of power.

 

• 1860 (Option 4): The transfer had already taken place by 1858; 1860 is incorrect.

question: According to census 2001, sex ratio is ______ females per 1000 males.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 933.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Census of India, 2001, the national sex ratio was 933 females per 1000 males. (जनगणना 2001 — लिंगानुपात 933)

 

• This marked an improvement over the Census 1991 figure of 927 females per 1000 males.

 

• The sex ratio subsequently rose further to 943 females per 1000 males as per the Census of India, 2011.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, Kerala had the highest sex ratio among states (1084), while Haryana had the lowest (879).

 

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) is tracked separately and has generally been a matter of concern due to its decline over recent censuses.

 

NOTE

 

• 943 (Option 1): This is the sex ratio figure from Census 2011, not 2001.

 

• 923 (Option 2): Not the correct 2001 census figure.

 

• 913 (Option 4): Not the correct 2001 census figure.

question: The Central Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed in Lok Sabha in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is August.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Central Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed by the Lok Sabha in August 2022. (केंद्रीय विश्वविद्यालय (संशोधन) विधेयक, 2022 — अगस्त 2022)

 

• The Bill amended the Central Universities Act, 2009, to convert the Central Sanskrit Universities/institutions and other central institutions and to establish/rename certain central universities, including provisions related to institutions such as the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya.

 

• It was subsequently passed to complete the parliamentary process for these institutional changes in 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Central universities in India are established or declared under an Act of Parliament and are funded by the University Grants Commission (UGC).

 

• A further Central Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced later to add more institutions to the schedule of central universities.

 

NOTE

 

• July (Option 2): Not the month in which this Bill was passed in the Lok Sabha.

 

• November (Option 3): Incorrect month for this Bill's passage.

 

• September (Option 4): Incorrect month for this Bill's passage.

question: Which city is called the ‘Manchester of India’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ahmedabad, in Gujarat, is popularly known as the 'Manchester of India' because of its large number of cotton textile mills, drawing a parallel with Manchester, England, historically a global hub of the cotton textile industry. (अहमदाबाद — भारत का मैनचेस्टर)

 

• Ahmedabad's textile industry grew rapidly from the late 19th century onward, making it one of India's leading centres for cotton spinning and weaving.

 

• The city, founded by Sultan Ahmed Shah in 1411, sits on the banks of the Sabarmati River.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kanpur is sometimes referred to as the 'Manchester of the East' or 'Leather City of the World' owing to its industrial base.

 

• Ahmedabad was also India's first UNESCO World Heritage City, recognised in 2017.

 

NOTE

 

• Ludhiana (Option 1): Known as the 'Manchester of India' in some contexts for its woollen hosiery industry, but the more standard and widely used answer for this classic nickname is Ahmedabad, historically tied to cotton textiles.

 

• Visakhapatnam (Option 2): Known as a major port city, not for this textile-based nickname.

 

• Hyderabad (Option 3): Known for IT and pharma industries, not for this nickname.

question: Which of the following is used in photography?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium thiosulphate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium thiosulphate (Na₂S₂O₃), commonly called 'hypo', is used in photography as a fixer, to dissolve unreacted silver halide from photographic film/paper after development. (सोडियम थायोसल्फेट — फोटोग्राफी में फिक्सर)

 

• By removing the undeveloped silver salts, hypo stabilises the image and prevents further darkening upon exposure to light.

 

• Sodium thiosulphate is also used in volumetric (iodometric) titrations in analytical chemistry and as an antidote for cyanide poisoning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Silver bromide (AgBr) is the light-sensitive compound coated on photographic film that reacts to light to form the latent image.

 

• Sodium thiosulphate is also used in water treatment to remove excess chlorine (dechlorination).

 

NOTE

 

• Sodium bicarbonate (Option 1): Common baking soda, used in cooking and as an antacid, not in photographic fixing.

 

• Sodium hydroxide (Option 3): A strong base (caustic soda) used in soap-making and various industrial processes, not for fixing photographs.

 

• Sodium sulphate (Option 4): Used in the manufacture of detergents and glass, not as a photographic fixer.

question: Who among the following rulers appointed Ladha and Pira, two gardeners to high administrative post?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Tughluq.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq was known for his unconventional administrative experiments, including appointing people of humble/low social origin — such as barbers, cooks and gardeners — to high administrative posts; among these were the gardeners Ladha and Pira. (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक — निम्न वर्ग के व्यक्तियों की नियुक्ति)

 

• The 14th-century chronicler Ziauddin Barani, in his work Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi, records such appointments as evidence of the Sultan's radical and often criticised administrative policies.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughluq is also remembered for other bold (and often failed) measures such as the transfer of capital to Daulatabad and the introduction of token currency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muhammad bin Tughluq is often called an 'ill-starred idealist' by historians for his ambitious but poorly executed reforms.

 

• His successor, Firuz Shah Tughluq, is noted for reversing many of these harsh measures and undertaking large public works instead.

 

NOTE

 

• Khizr Khan (Option 1): Founder of the Sayyid dynasty, unrelated to these appointments.

 

• Bahlul Lodi (Option 3): Founder of the Lodi dynasty, unrelated to these appointments.

 

• Iltutmish (Option 4): A prominent Slave (Mamluk) dynasty Sultan, unrelated to these appointments.

question: Pivoting is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Basketball.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pivoting is a fundamental basketball technique in which a player who is holding the ball keeps one foot (the 'pivot foot') fixed at a point on the floor while moving the other foot in any direction. (पिवोटिंग — बास्केटबॉल)

 

• It allows a player to change direction, protect the ball from a defender, or find a passing/shooting angle without committing a travelling violation.

 

• Basketball was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 in the USA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A basketball court is divided into two halves, each with a hoop/basket mounted at 10 feet (3.05 m) height.

 

• Other key basketball terms include dribbling, rebound, free throw and dunk.

 

NOTE

 

• Hockey (Option 1): Uses terms like dribbling, tackle and penalty corner; pivoting is not a defining hockey term.

 

• Volleyball (Option 2): Uses terms like spike, dig and block; not associated with pivoting.

 

• Badminton (Option 3): Uses terms like smash, serve and rally; not associated with pivoting.

question: Who has been appointed as the country’s second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anil Chauhan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• General Anil Chauhan (Retd.) was appointed as India's second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), taking charge on 30 September 2022. (जनरल अनिल चौहान — भारत के दूसरे चीफ ऑफ डिफेंस स्टाफ)

 

• The post had remained vacant since the death of India's first CDS, General Bipin Rawat, in a helicopter crash in December 2021.

 

• As CDS, General Chauhan also heads the Department of Military Affairs (DMA) and acts as the principal military adviser to the Defence Minister.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The post of CDS was created in December 2019 on the recommendation of a committee following the Kargil Review Committee's suggestions.

 

• General Anil Chauhan previously served as the Eastern Army Commander and also as a National Security Adviser (NSA)-related security post before this appointment.

 

NOTE

 

• Manoj Kumar (Option 2): Not the officer appointed as second CDS.

 

• R Dinesh (Option 3): Not the officer appointed as second CDS.

 

• Sanjay Agarwal (Option 4): Not the officer appointed as second CDS.

question: In all AIBA Boxing competitions, the rest time between each round is ________ minutes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In AIBA (International Boxing Association) competitions, each round of boxing lasts 3 minutes, with a rest interval of 1 minute between successive rounds. (एआईबीए मुक्केबाजी — राउंड के बीच 1 मिनट का विश्राम)

 

• A standard men's Olympic/amateur bout typically consists of 3 rounds of 3 minutes each, separated by these 1-minute rest periods.

 

• AIBA, now known as the International Boxing Association (IBA), was founded in 1946 and is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In professional boxing, bouts can extend up to 12 rounds, but the standard 1-minute rest between rounds remains the same.

 

• Boxing has been part of the Olympic Games since 1904 (men) and 2012 (women, at London).

 

NOTE

 

• 2 (Option 2): Not the standard rest period between rounds.

 

• 3 (Option 3): This is the duration of a round itself, not the rest period.

 

• 5 (Option 4): Not the standard rest period between rounds.

question: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence is a_______________ in the Indian Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is fundamental duty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(i) of the Indian Constitution lists it as a Fundamental Duty of every citizen 'to safeguard public property and to abjure violence'. (मूल कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are listed under Part IVA.

 

• Originally 10 duties were added; an 11th duty (regarding the duty of parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6–14) was added later by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties in India are inspired by Article 51 of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet) Constitution.

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be directly enforced by courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Social ethic (Option 2): Not a formal constitutional category; this duty is specifically classified as a Fundamental Duty.

 

• Fundamental right (Option 3): Fundamental Rights are listed in Part III; this particular provision is a Fundamental Duty in Part IVA, not a Right.

 

• Directive principle of state policy (Option 4): DPSPs (Part IV) are guidelines for the State, not duties of citizens; this provision is a citizen's duty, not a DPSP.

question: In honour of an Indian musician, the US state of Massachusetts proclaimed 20 April as __________ in 1984.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amjad Ali Khan Day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1984, the Governor of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Michael S. Dukakis, proclaimed 20 April as 'Amjad Ali Khan Day', honouring the celebrated Indian sarod maestro Ustad Amjad Ali Khan. (अमजद अली खान दिवस — मैसाचुसेट्स, 1984)

 

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is one of India's foremost sarod players, belonging to the Senia Bangash gharana, and has performed extensively across the world since the 1960s.

 

• He has been honoured with India's major civilian awards, including the Padma Shri (1975), Padma Bhushan (1991) and Padma Vibhushan (2001).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amjad Ali Khan is also a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1989) for his contribution to Hindustani classical music.

 

• His sons, Amaan Ali Bangash and Ayaan Ali Bangash, have also become notable sarod players, continuing the family's musical lineage.

 

NOTE

 

• Sakhawat Hussain Day (Option 1): Not the day proclaimed by Massachusetts in 1984; Ustad Sakhawat Hussain Khan was a noted sarod player of an earlier generation.

 

• Sharan Rani Backliwal Day (Option 2): Sharan Rani Backliwal was a pioneering female sarod player and Padma Bhushan awardee, but it is Amjad Ali Khan, not her, who was honoured by this specific 1984 Massachusetts proclamation.

 

• Allauddin Khan Day (Option 4): Baba Allauddin Khan founded the Maihar gharana and taught Ravi Shankar and Ali Akbar Khan, but this 1984 Massachusetts proclamation honoured Amjad Ali Khan, not him.

question: Rukmini Devi Arundale is the exponent of which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale was a pioneering exponent and reviver of Bharatanatyam, and she founded the renowned dance and arts academy Kalakshetra in Chennai in 1936. (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल — भरतनाट्यम, कलाक्षेत्र)

 

• She is credited with giving Bharatanatyam a respectable, structured stage form and removing its earlier association with the devadasi (sadir) tradition, presenting it as a refined classical art.

 

• She was also a noted theosophist and animal rights activist, and served as a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1956 and declined the offer of the post of President of India in 1977.

 

• Kalakshetra Foundation continues to be one of India's most prestigious institutions for classical dance and music training.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipuri (Option 2): Associated with exponents such as Guru Bipin Singh, not Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

• Sattriya (Option 3): The classical dance form of Assam, associated with the Vaishnavite Sattras, not Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

• Odissi (Option 4): Associated with exponents such as Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, not Rukmini Devi Arundale.

question: In which group are the non-metal elements placed in a vertical column on the right side of the periodic table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Group 17.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Group 17 of the modern periodic table, positioned on the right side, consists of the halogens — fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine and astatine — which are all non-metals (astatine is a metalloid/radioactive). (समूह 17 — हैलोजन तत्व)

 

• Halogens are highly reactive non-metals that readily gain one electron to form -1 anions, and they exist in various states — fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a liquid, and iodine is a solid at room temperature.

 

• Group 18, further to the right, contains the noble gases, which are largely inert non-metals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The periodic table has 18 groups (vertical columns) and 7 periods (horizontal rows), with non-metals concentrated towards the upper right, metals towards the left and centre, and metalloids along the dividing staircase line.

 

• Halogens combine with alkali metals (Group 1) to form salts, giving the term 'halogen' its meaning (Greek for 'salt-producer').

 

NOTE

 

• Group 1 (Option 1): Contains the alkali metals (e.g., sodium, potassium), which are metals, not non-metals.

 

• Group 2 (Option 2): Contains the alkaline earth metals (e.g., calcium, magnesium), which are metals.

 

• Group 3 (Option 4): Contains transition metals (e.g., scandium, yttrium), which are metals.

question: _________ measures the aggregate production of final goods and services taking place within the domestic economy during a year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross domestic product.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the total market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country during a given year, regardless of who owns the factors of production. (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद — GDP)

 

• GDP is a territorial concept — it excludes net income earned by residents from abroad, unlike GNP-based measures.

 

• GDP is widely used as the primary indicator of a country's overall economic size and growth rate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, GDP estimates are compiled and released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

 

• GDP can be calculated using three approaches: the production (output) method, the income method, and the expenditure method.

 

NOTE

 

• Gross National income (Option 1): GNI measures income earned by a country's residents/nationals, including net income from abroad, not confined to domestic production alone.

 

• Net national product (Option 3): NNP equals GNP minus depreciation, and is a national (not purely domestic) production/income measure.

 

• National income at factor price (Option 4): This is NNP valued at factor cost, a related but distinct national-income measure, not the domestic-production concept described here.

question: Nuts, vegetable oil and fish are good source of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Healthy fats.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nuts, vegetable oils and fish (especially fatty fish) are rich sources of healthy (unsaturated) fats, including monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids such as omega-3 fatty acids. (स्वस्थ वसा — नट्स, वनस्पति तेल, मछली)

 

• These unsaturated fats are considered beneficial for heart health, in contrast to saturated and trans fats found in many animal fats and processed foods.

 

• Omega-3 fatty acids, abundant in fatty fish like salmon and mackerel, are associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular disease.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Essential fatty acids cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained through diet.

 

• A balanced diet includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals in appropriate proportions for overall health.

 

NOTE

 

• Carbohydrates (Option 1): Mainly obtained from cereals, grains, fruits and sugars, not primarily from nuts/oils/fish.

 

• Minerals (Option 2): Obtained from a variety of foods like dairy, leafy vegetables and fruits; not the primary nutrient these foods are known for.

 

• Proteins (Option 4): While nuts and fish do contain protein, the defining nutritional characteristic being tested here (shared by all three — nuts, vegetable oil and fish) is their fat content.

question: In which of the following years was the Indian National Congress split into two groups named as Moderates and Extremists?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1907.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National Congress split into two factions — the Moderates and the Extremists — at its Surat Session in 1907, an event known as the 'Surat Split'. (सूरत विभाजन, 1907 — उदारवादी और उग्रवादी)

 

• The split arose from differences over goals and methods: Moderates (like Gopal Krishna Gokhale) favoured constitutional agitation, while Extremists (like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Lala Lajpat Rai — the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio) favoured more assertive, mass-based methods including Swadeshi and boycott.

 

• The immediate trigger was disagreement over the choice of the Congress president for the session, which led to chaos and the formal division of the party.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The two factions reunited at the Lucknow Session of the Congress in 1916, the same session that saw the Lucknow Pact between the Congress and the Muslim League.

 

• The Swadeshi Movement (1905) against the Partition of Bengal was a major backdrop to the rise of Extremist politics.

 

NOTE

 

• 1895 (Option 1): Not the year of the Moderate-Extremist split.

 

• 1899 (Option 2): Not the year of the Moderate-Extremist split.

 

• 1904 (Option 4): Not the year of the Moderate-Extremist split; it occurred in 1907.

question: Who among the following contemporary style dancers was the first Indian dancer to receive the dance WEB Europe Scholarship? He/She also won the 2002 American Choreography Award for his/her work in the movie ‘Lagaan’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Terence Lewis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Terence Lewis was the first Indian dancer to receive the 'dance WEB Europe Scholarship', which allowed him to train in contemporary dance techniques in Europe. (टेरेंस लुईस — समकालीन नृत्य कोरियोग्राफर)

 

• He also won the 2002 American Choreography Award for his choreography work in the film 'Lagaan', along with other choreographers associated with the film.

 

• Terence Lewis is a well-known contemporary dance choreographer in India and has trained under institutions abroad before establishing his own dance company and academy in Mumbai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Terence Lewis has also served as a judge on popular Indian dance reality television shows.

 

• 'Lagaan' (2001), directed by Ashutosh Gowariker, was itself nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

 

NOTE

 

• Ashley Lobo (Option 2): A noted contemporary dance choreographer in India, but not the recipient of this specific scholarship/award combination described here.

 

• Padmini Chettur (Option 3): A well-known contemporary dancer/choreographer, but not associated with this specific scholarship and 'Lagaan' award.

 

• Shakti Mohan (Option 4): A popular dancer known from television dance reality shows, not associated with this specific scholarship and 'Lagaan' award.
